### 1 — Scene
A mixed appetizer/meat plate: a fresh shrimp spring roll, bone-in cooked meat, additional meat pieces, and breaded fried shrimp. Some identifications are approximate.

### 2 — Vessel
Likely a **26 cm dinner plate**.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
The yellow coating on the bone-in meat is included in its cooked energy estimate. No separate pool of sauce or oil is visible.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × average height = volume | Bulk density | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Fresh shrimp-and-lettuce rice-paper roll | 11% | 58 × 2.0 = 116 ml | 0.90 | 105 g | 125 | 131 kcal |
| Braised bone-in meat, likely lamb, with coating—edible portion | 12% | 64 × 2.0 = 128 ml | 0.95 | 122 g | 270 | 329 kcal |
| Small cooked beef piece at upper right | 5% | 27 × 1.5 = 40 ml | 0.95 | 38 g | 250 | 95 kcal |
| Two browned ground-meat pieces near bottom | 9% | 48 × 1.3 = 62 ml | 0.95 | 59 g | 260 | 153 kcal |
| Breaded fried shrimp on right | 12% | 64 × 1.3 = 83 ml | 0.85 | 71 g | 280 | 199 kcal |

### 4 — Coverage check
Edible items cover approximately **49%** of the plate. The exposed bone occupies another **3%**, giving **52% total coverage**, consistent with the broad empty rim and gaps. The inedible bone is excluded from the weight and energy totals.

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **395 g of edible food and 910 kcal** is plausible for this partially covered plate of relatively dense meat and fried foods. Portion thickness and uncertain meat identification could shift the estimate by roughly 20–25%.
